mainTopic: The size and shape rules for carrying in an enclosed garden or קרפף, and how sowing affects a קרפף fenced for living
overview: The גמרא continues explaining the משנה about carrying on שבת in a fenced garden or קרפף. First it shows that רבי עקיבא and the תנא קמא differ by a tiny amount of area. It then defines בית סאתים as the size of the חצר המשכן and learns from a פסוק that this area may be squared off to about 70 by 70 אמות. Next it reconciles two versions of רבי אליעזר's view and shows how he still differs from רבי יוסי. שמואל is reported as ruling like both רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא, and the גמרא explains that the הלכה takes both leniencies. A ברייתא then teaches that a large קרפף fenced for living becomes forbidden if most of it is sown, but not if most of it is planted with trees. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits this to a sown part bigger than בית סאתים. The גמרא links his view to רבי שמעון and then begins to reject that link, an argument that finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא seems identical to the first opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges that רבי עקיבא's stated size of 70 and a remainder by 70 and a remainder seems to repeat the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is complaining that רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה seems to add nothing new about the garden's size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the תנא קמא (רבי יהודה בן בבא) and רבי עקיבא limit the garden to about בית סאתים. They argue about whether a watchman's hut or a dwelling is needed. On the size itself they seem to agree, so why does רבי עקיבא state the measurement again?

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
תנא who gives the size of seventy and a remainder by seventy and a remainder in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is only about the size of the garden. It is not about the watchman's hut or dwelling, where the two clearly disagree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva is the same as the first Tanna!
phrases.notes: This is really a challenge: the two of them seem to be saying the same thing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of רבי עקיבא's clause in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's measurement of seventy cubits and a remainder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both opinions allow the same area, repeating the measurement is redundant.

steps.title: They differ by a tiny amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ by a tiny amount, citing a ברייתא of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: a tiny amount. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says, a tiny amount exists beyond seventy cubits and a remainder, and the Sages did not give it a measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the opinions are not identical. They differ by a very small sliver of area, as רבי יהודה's ברייתא shows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A true square of בית סאתים has a side a tiny bit longer than 'seventy cubits and a remainder.' According to the גמרא, the תנא קמא allows the full בית סאתים. רבי עקיבא allows only 70 and a remainder squared, which is a hair smaller. The Sages never fixed this tiny extra amount because it is too small to measure precisely.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Seventy cubits and a remainder (about two-thirds of a cubit)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'seventy and a remainder' is a close approximation of the square root of בית סאתים, not an exact figure.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: a tiny amount.
As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר מוּעָט יֵשׁ עַל שִׁבְעִים אַמָּה וְשִׁירַיִם,
phrases.english: There is a tiny amount beyond seventy cubits and a remainder,
phrases.notes: The true side of a square בית סאתים is slightly longer.

phrases.english: and the Sages did not give it a measurement.
phrases.notes: It is too small to state precisely.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference (נפקא מינה) between the opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both opinions allow exactly the same area.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא allows the full בית סאתים. רבי עקיבא's 70 and a remainder squared is smaller by a tiny amount.

steps.title: A בית סאתים equals the courtyard of the Mishkan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defines the area of בית סאתים as the size of the חצר המשכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the measurement of סאתים? Like the חצר המשכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how big a בית סאתים is and answers right away: the size of the חצר המשכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חצר המשכן was 100 by 50 cubits, which is 5,000 square cubits. Squared off, each side is about 70 and two-thirds cubits plus a tiny bit. This explains where the 'seventy and a remainder' figure comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Two סאה, short for בית סאתים: the area needed to sow two סאה of seed
The courtyard of the משכן (100 by 50 cubits)

steps.whatToRemember: בית סאתים = 5,000 square cubits = the חצר המשכן. Squared, each side is about 70⅔ cubits plus a tiny bit.

phrases.english: And how much is the measurement of two se'ah?
Like the courtyard of the Mishkan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the measurement used in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area of בית סאתים equals the חצר המשכן, 5,000 square cubits.

steps.title: What is the source for this measurement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the חצר המשכן is the standard, and that it may be squared off.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for a source and will next bring a פסוק to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having equated בית סאתים with the חצר המשכן, the גמרא now wants a scriptural basis. It wants to know why the Mishkan is the model, and why the rectangle may be reshaped into a square.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words derived? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the definition in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for using the חצר המשכן as the measure, and for squaring it off.

steps.title: רב יהודה derives the square shape from the verse about the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns from the פסוק that the 100-by-50 area of the חצר המשכן may be rearranged into a square: take a 50-by-50 block and wrap the other 50 around it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The verse says, 'The length of the courtyard is a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty by fifty.' The תורה is saying: take a fifty-by-fifty square, and surround it with the other fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from Step 4. He shows where we learn that the חצר המשכן is the standard measure and that its area may be reshaped into a square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard is 100 by 50, which is 5,000 square אמות. The odd wording 'fifty by fifty' hints that we should think of it as a 50-by-50 square, with the other 2,500 square אמות spread around it as strips. The result is a square of about 70 and a remainder on each side, which is exactly the measurement in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Courtyard (here, the courtyard around the משכן)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source that turns the long rectangle of the חצר המשכן into the '70 and a remainder by 70 and a remainder' square that defines a בית סאתים.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Surround with fifty' does not mean adding 50 אמות to each side. It means the leftover 2,500 square אמות is spread thinly around the 50-by-50 square, so each side grows only to about 70.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
For the verse states:
"The length of the courtyard shall be a hundred cubits,
and the breadth fifty by fifty."
phrases.notes: The double 'fifty' is the hint רב יהודה builds on.

phrases.english: The Torah said:
Take fifty (a 50-by-50 square),
and surround it with the other fifty.
phrases.notes: The remaining 50-by-50 area is spread around the square, giving about 70 by 70.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4 about the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'fifty by fifty' teaches that the 5,000 square אמות of the courtyard may be squared off: a 50-by-50 square surrounded by the remaining fifty.

steps.title: What does the verse plainly mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the verse is being read as a hint for squaring off the area, what does it mean in its simple sense?
steps.simpleTranslation: The plain meaning of the verse, what is it talking about?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the simple meaning of 'fifty by fifty,' since a courtyard 50 wide cannot simply be '50 by 50.' This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה used the words as a hint, but the פסוק still needs a straightforward meaning about the actual courtyard. The גמרא wants to know what 'fifty by fifty' describes in the real structure of the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain, simple meaning of the verse

phrases.english: The plain meaning of the verse, about what is it written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רב יהודה's reading by asking for the verse's literal sense.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The simple meaning of 'fifty by fifty' in the description of the courtyard.

steps.title: אביי explains the layout of the משכן inside its courtyard
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the משכן stood so that a 50-by-50 open space was in front of it, with 20 אמות on each of its other sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Place the משכן at the edge of fifty, so that there are fifty cubits in front of it and twenty cubits on every other side.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the simple meaning of the פסוק: 'fifty by fifty' describes the open square in front of the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן was 30 long and 10 wide, and the courtyard was 100 by 50. Across the width: 20 + 10 + 20 = 50. Along the length: 50 in front + 30 for the משכן + 20 behind = 100. So the front section of the courtyard was a 50-by-50 square, which is what 'fifty by fifty' literally describes.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק has two layers. Its simple meaning (אביי) is the 50-by-50 space in front of the משכן. Its hint (רב יהודה) is that the courtyard's area may be squared off to about 70 by 70.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Position the Tabernacle at the edge of fifty,
so that there are fifty cubits in front of it,
and twenty cubits on every other side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַעֲמֵד מִשְׁכָּן עַל שְׂפַת חֲמִשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Fifty by fifty' describes the 50-by-50 open space in front of the משכן, with 20 אמות on the other sides.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next part of the משנה: רבי אליעזר's ruling about an enclosure whose length is greater than its width.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: If its length was, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the opening words of רבי אליעזר's statement in the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says that if the length is greater than the width, even by one אמה, you may not carry inside. The גמרא quotes only the first words (כו׳ means 'etc.') so that it can compare them to a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If its length was, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line: greater than its width, even by one cubit, one may not carry inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיְתָה אׇרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה after the source discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: an enclosure whose length exceeds its width, even by one אמה, does not allow carrying inside.

steps.title: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר differently
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר as forbidding carrying only when the length is more than double the width, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, if its length is more than double its width, even by one cubit, one may not carry inside it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's version of רבי אליעזר with a ברייתא that quotes him differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the משנה, a length that exceeds the width by even one אמה is already forbidden. According to the ברייתא, there is no problem until the length passes double the width. These are two different limits for the same תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If its length is more
than double its width,
even by one cubit,
one may not carry inside it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of רבי אליעזר quoted in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי אליעזר in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה forbids carrying once the length is greater than the width at all. The ברייתא forbids only when the length is more than double the width. The same תנא cannot hold both.

steps.title: The משנה also means 'more than double'
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי answers that the משנה's version of רבי אליעזר is also talking about a length more than double the width.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: When we learned the משנה too, we learned 'more than double its width.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי resolves the contradiction by reading the משנה as matching the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real disagreement between the sources. The משנה is shorthand for 'more than double its width.' So רבי אליעזר's limit is double the width, and passing it by even one אמה forbids carrying.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
When we learned the Mishnah too,
we learned 'more than double its width.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה to match the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's רבי אליעזר forbids any length greater than the width.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's רבי אליעזר also forbids only a length more than double the width.

steps.title: Then רבי אליעזר says the same as רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if רבי אליעזר allows up to double, his view seems identical to רבי יוסי's, who also allows carrying even when the length is double the width.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as רבי יוסי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ביבי's answer, because it makes רבי אליעזר's view the same as רבי יוסי's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי says you may carry even if the length is double the width. If רבי אליעזר forbids only beyond double, the two תנאים seem to agree. Then why does the משנה list them as separate opinions?

phrases.english: If so,
this is the same as Rabbi Yosei?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ביבי בר אביי's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי אליעזר's limit is double the width, he matches רבי יוסי, who permits up to double. Two separately listed opinions would then be identical.

steps.title: The difference: a square measured with its diagonal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי still disagree about a square measured the way the חכמים measured squares, including the diagonal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the square that the Sages squared.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 11. It shows a case where רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי really do disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked whether רבי אליעזר now says the same thing as רבי יוסי, since both allow carrying up to double. The answer is that they still argue about a square measured with its diagonal, the way the חכמים calculated squares. Following רבינו חננאל: if the diagonal is more than double the width, רבי אליעזר forbids carrying, but רבי יוסי allows it, because the real length is not more than double.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them; a practical case where two views give different results
The way the חכמים calculated squares, including the diagonal

steps.confusionAlert: The two views are not identical. They agree on the basic shape of length and width, but they disagree once you also look at the diagonal. There are other explanations of this line as well, for example רש"י's. The explanation here follows רבינו חננאל.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא points out a practical difference between two views.

phrases.english: the square that the Sages squared.
phrases.notes: A square measured along its diagonal, the way the חכמים calculated it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 11, which claimed רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי would be identical.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a practical difference (נפקא מינה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once רבי אליעזר allows up to double, he seems to say exactly what רבי יוסי says.
steps.terutzMaskana: They still disagree about a square whose diagonal is more than double the width.

steps.title: Two reports of שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי יוסי's view in the משנה and brings two reports of שמואל's ruling: one follows רבי יוסי, the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי יוסי says' and so on. It was stated: רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. And רב ביבי said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי יוסי's view. It then reports that שמואל's ruling was passed down in two different versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יוסי says you may carry even if the length is double the width. רבי עקיבא says no watchman's hut or dwelling is needed, as long as the area is 70 and a bit by 70 and a bit. רב יוסף and רב ביבי both quote רב יהודה in the name of שמואל, yet they report different rulings. This looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; introduces a statement or dispute of אמוראים
The practical law follows this view
תנא in the משנה who does not require a hut or dwelling, only the right size

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the next line of the משנה.

phrases.english: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said
that Shmuel said: the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.
And Rav Beivai said that Rav Yehuda said
that Shmuel said: the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר discussion and starts a new topic: the final הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל is reported as ruling like רבי יוסי, and also reported as ruling like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Both rulings are lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two reports do not contradict each other, because both rule leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both of them are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the apparent contradiction from Step 13. It says both rulings point in the lenient direction, so שמואל could have said both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי and רבי עקיבא are lenient about different issues. רבי יוסי is lenient about the shape, allowing a length up to double the width. רבי עקיבא is lenient about use, requiring no hut or dwelling. So following both at once is not a contradiction. You simply take both leniencies.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think שמואל picked one תנא over the other. He accepts each one's leniency on a different issue.

phrases.english: And both of them are lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent conflict between the two reports in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Harmonization: each ruling teaches a separate leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of שמואל contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are true. The הלכה follows each תנא's leniency.

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבי עקיבא was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if we had only the ruling like רבי יוסי, we might have thought a watchman's hut or dwelling is still required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary. For if it had taught us only that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, I would have said that carrying is allowed only if there is a watchman's hut or a dwelling. So it teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכא, explaining why both rulings had to be said. This half explains why the ruling like רבי עקיבא was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי only talks about the shape of the enclosure. He never says that a hut or dwelling is unnecessary. So if we heard only 'הלכה כרבי יוסי', we might still require a hut or dwelling, like the earlier views in the משנה. The ruling like רבי עקיבא teaches that no such structure is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; explains why two seemingly overlapping statements are both needed
I would have thought; the mistaken assumption we would otherwise make

phrases.english: And it was necessary,
for if it had taught us the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei,
I would have said: only if there is
a watchman's booth or a dwelling.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: So it teaches us the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands Step 14 by showing that each ruling adds something. This half covers רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: explains why both statements are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruling like רבי יוסי alone might still require a hut or dwelling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ruling like רבי עקיבא shows no hut or dwelling is needed.

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבי יוסי was needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that if we had only the ruling like רבי עקיבא, we might have forbidden a long, narrow enclosure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only that the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, I would have said that a long and narrow enclosure is not allowed. So it teaches us that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by explaining why the ruling like רבי יוסי was also needed. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא speaks of an area of 70 and a bit by 70 and a bit, which sounds like a square. If we heard only his ruling, we might think a long, narrow enclosure is forbidden. The ruling like רבי יוסי teaches that the length may reach double the width.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, you may carry in an enclosure of about a בית סאתים even without a hut or dwelling, which is רבי עקיבא's leniency. You may also carry there even if its length is up to double its width, which is רבי יוסי's leniency. The הלכה takes both leniencies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא works: when two rulings seem to clash, it shows that each one teaches a separate leniency, so the final הלכה combines them.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva,
I would have said that a long and narrow one is not allowed.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: So it teaches us the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the צריכא begun in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both reports of שמואל are needed. Together they permit carrying without a hut or dwelling, and in a shape up to double length.

steps.title: A large enclosure that is mostly sown becomes like a garden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a קרפף bigger than בית סאתים, fenced for living, becomes forbidden for carrying if most of it is sown with seed crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קרפף that is bigger than בית סאתים and was fenced in for living: if most of it was sown, it is like a garden, and carrying in it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a big enclosure that was fenced in for living, and later most of it was sown with seed crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a big קרפף fenced for living is allowed for carrying, whatever its size. But people sow seed crops in gardens away from the house, not where they live. So once most of it is sown, it loses its 'living area' status and counts as a גינה, which is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An enclosed open area, such as a yard or field, outside the house
An area big enough to sow two סאה of seed (5,000 square אמות). This is the size limit for carrying in an enclosure not fenced for living.
Fenced in for the purpose of living there
Was sown with seed crops, such as grain or vegetables
A garden. It is not a living area.

phrases.english: A karpef that is larger than two beit se'a
which was enclosed for the purpose of dwelling,
phrases.notes: Because it was fenced for living, carrying is normally allowed no matter how big it is.

phrases.english: if most of it was sown with seeds
it is like a garden, and it is forbidden to carry there.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַרְפֵּף שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם שֶׁהוּקַּף לְדִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: what happens to a קרפף fenced for living when its use changes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A large קרפף fenced for living that is mostly sown is treated like a גינה, and carrying is forbidden.

steps.title: A large enclosure that is mostly planted with trees stays like a courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if most of the קרפף is planted with trees, it is like a חצר, and carrying is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If most of it was planted with trees, it is like a courtyard, and carrying is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case: most of the enclosure was planted with trees instead of sown with seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often plant trees even in the courtyard next to their house. So trees do not take away the 'living area' status. The enclosure stays like a חצר, and carrying remains allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard next to the house, which counts as a living area

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נזרע and נטע. נזרע means seed crops, and the result is forbidden. נטע means trees, and the result is permitted.

phrases.english: If he planted most of it with trees
it is like a courtyard, and carrying is permitted.
phrases.notes: People plant trees in courtyards too, so this does not change the living-area status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 17: trees instead of seed crops.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A large קרפף fenced for living that is mostly planted with trees stays like a חצר, and carrying is permitted.

steps.title: The sown part forbids carrying only if it is bigger than בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע limits the ברייתא. The sown part makes carrying forbidden only if the sown part itself is bigger than בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the case where 'most of it was sown,' רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: We only said this when the sown part is bigger than בית סאתים. But if it is only בית סאתים, carrying is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows the forbidden case of the ברייתא from step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'most' of the enclosure is not enough. The sown section itself must be bigger than בית סאתים to cause a problem. A garden of up to בית סאתים is not too big to carry in. So it can join with the rest of the קרפף, and the whole area stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, an אמורא
We only said this in the case of... (a formula that limits a ruling)

phrases.english: Regarding 'most of it was sown,'
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא to show which ruling is being limited.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: We only said this when the sown part is larger than two beit se'a.
But if it is only two beit se'a, carrying is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא יוֹתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the forbidden ruling of step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sown part forbids carrying in the קרפף only if the sown part itself is bigger than בית סאתים. Up to בית סאתים, carrying is permitted.

steps.title: Whose view is רב הונא following? רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא רב הונא's limit follows, and answers: רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this follow? It follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind רב הונא's ruling and names רבי שמעון. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's ruling needs the sown garden and the rest of the קרפף to count as one domain, even though they have different status. The גמרא points to רבי שמעון as the תנא who holds this kind of view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose view does this follow?
רבי שמעון בר יוחאי, a תנא

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? In accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finds the source behind רב הונא's ruling from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רב הונא's leniency follow?

steps.title: רבי שמעון: roofs, courtyards and enclosures are one domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. רבי שמעון holds that roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות are all one domain for utensils that were there when שבת began, but not for utensils that were in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה, רבי שמעון says: Roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות are all one domain for utensils that were in them when שבת began. They are not one domain for utensils that were inside the house when שבת began.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that proves רבי שמעון's view, which supports רב הונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says that different open areas, even with different status, join together as one domain for carrying utensils that started שבת there. So too, a sown garden of up to בית סאתים and the unsown part of the קרפף join as one domain, and the garden does not make the rest forbidden. The limit is utensils that started שבת inside the house, since the house is a real dwelling.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
That 'rested' there, meaning they were in that place when שבת began

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא's proposal: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limit (the sown part must be bigger than בית סאתים) follows רבי שמעון, who says roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות join as one domain for utensils that started שבת there. The next step pushes back on this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא tries to ground רב הונא's limit in a known תנאי position about different areas joining into one domain. The next step challenges whether this proof really works.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna, Rabbi Shimon says:
Roofs and courtyards alike
and karpeifot alike, are all one domain
for utensils that were in them when Shabbat began,
phrases.notes: This holds even if the utensils belong to different people, and no עירוב is needed.

phrases.english: but not for utensils that were inside the house when Shabbat began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the משנה behind the answer 'רבי שמעון' in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that a sown section of up to בית סאתים does not make the rest of the קרפף forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי שמעון says that roofs, courtyards and קרפיפות are one domain for utensils that started שבת in them.

steps.title: Even רבי שמעון may treat the small unsown part as secondary to the sown majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the claim from Step 20 that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limit follows רבי שמעון. It argues that even according to רבי שמעון, once most of the קרפף is sown, the remaining minority is treated as secondary to the sown majority, so רבי שמעון's view cannot support the leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to רבי שמעון, since most of the קרפף is sown, that small remaining part is... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back against its own last move, the claim that רב הונא's limit must follow רבי שמעון. This line opens the rejection, and its ending comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof relied on רבי שמעון treating courtyards and קרפיפות as one domain. The rejection says that this does not settle the question. Even רבי שמעון may agree that when most of the area is sown, the small unsown minority is pulled after the majority. If so, the earlier proof from רבי שמעון no longer works.

keyTerms.meaning: The minority, the small remaining part

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as a mild doubt about the proof. The גמרא is arguing that even רבי שמעון would not support רב הונא's leniency. Once most of the קרפף is sown, the small unsown part is drawn after the sown majority, so the whole קרפף counts as a garden bigger than בית סאתים, where carrying is forbidden. So רב הונא's ruling cannot rest on רבי שמעון. The argument finishes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Even according to Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is taking back the idea that this depends on רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: since most of it was sown,
phrases.notes: The majority of the קרפף has seed crops.

phrases.english: that minority becomes...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 21 that רב הונא's limit follows רבי שמעון.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's limit must follow רבי שמעון, based on the משנה from Step 21.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי שמעון's view about one shared domain does not prevent a sown majority from making the small unsown minority secondary to it.
